question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $28,$ the additive inverse of $7$ modulo $28$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $7$ modulo $28$ is the integer $0\le x<28$ such that

$$
x+7≡0\,(\text{mod}\,28).
$$

Notice that $-7+7≡0,$ so $x≡-7\,(\text{mod}\,28).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-7 & \,(\text{mod}\,28) \\  & ≡0-7 & \,(\text{mod}\,28) \\  & ≡28-7 & \,(\text{mod}\,28) \\  & ≡21 & \,(\text{mod}\,28)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $7$ modulo $28$ is $21.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
7+21≡28≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,28)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
